title: Leaving Baron Wilkins to build a band
summary: Declining a doubled salary because the manager Dude Adams wanted two men cut, he leaves after about fourteen months to be a bandleader.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Were you ever called upon to make any records, to appear in any records during that period?
Not until the next year. I had a chance to go to make records the next year.
Alright, first let's get to that. When did you leave Baron Wilkins? And how, under what circumstances?

I left Baron Wilkins after being there about a year and two or three months. And what happened -- Old Man Baron didn't want me to leave. But what happened, the dude wanted to cut the band down. Well as I knew in those days and as I feel today, the band was more important than me. See, cause I could have been a good pianist. But I stopped thinking about the piano and started working, now, towards having a good band. See, I thought I'd go farther with a band than I would with a piano. I used to be a composer. I used to with a lot of things.

So, when we left there, I didn't have a -- Old Man Baron told me, 'You're foolish for leaving here, son.' And he used a four letter word, but he said, 'Because you won't be out on the street two weeks before you won't know who the first musician

is you're quitting for. And if you stay, I will double your salary, but we'll cut you two men off -- down to five. Because that's what Dude wanted. Dude Adams was his manager. So I said, "No, no Mr. Baron. I appreciate what you're trying to offer me, but my idea is to have a band. Not to make a little more money." You see?

So, of course, I'd bought a house there, you see, and I'd paid $14,000. for it. Course, we made good money, no question bout that. But that wasn't important to me. My idea was to be a successful band leader.
